statement: Theoretical nuclear physics research on the reaction mechanisms that govern the formation of heavy and superheavy nuclei, using stochastic dynamics and uncertainty quantification.
intro_paragraphs: Research on the reaction mechanisms behind the synthesis of superheavy elements, using stochastic modelling, scientific computing and uncertainty quantification, with applications in machine learning and data engineering.

working.title: KEWPIE3
working.text: Development of computational tools for fusion–evaporation cross-section calculations, parameter calibration, sensitivity analysis, and uncertainty propagation.

working.title: Nuclear Reaction Dynamics
working.text: Langevin-based modelling of heavy-ion reactions, from fusion–evaporation to the synthesis of superheavy elements.

working.title: Scientific Computing
working.text: Development of computational workflows for parameter studies, distributed calculations, optimisation, and reproducible scientific analysis.

highlights.title: Nuclear Reaction Dynamics
highlights.text: I study the dynamics of heavy-ion reactions, with particular interest in fusion–evaporation reactions and the synthesis of superheavy elements: capture, compound-nucleus formation, survival, and their theoretical modelling.

highlights.title: Uncertainty Quantification
highlights.text: Investigation of model sensitivity, parameter variation, calibration, and uncertainty propagation in nuclear-reaction calculations.

technical_title: Scientific Computing, Data Science and Engineering
technical_text: I apply computational and data-driven methods to scientific problems, with interests spanning scientific software, high-performance computing, data analysis, machine learning, and reproducible computational workflows.

teaching_block.title: Teaching
teaching_block.text: I teach undergraduate physics at the University of Ghana, with an emphasis on clear conceptual development, quantitative reasoning, and problem-solving.

academic.title: Academic Profile
paragraphs: My academic background spans experimental and theoretical nuclear physics, scientific computing, and data-intensive research.

I completed my undergraduate studies at the University of Ghana before undertaking postgraduate training in theoretical nuclear physics in Europe and doctoral research on the synthesis of superheavy elements.

fh_headline: At the Edge of the Periodic Table
fh_sub: Investigating the reaction dynamics of superheavy-element synthesis at the limits of nuclear stability
fh_intro: How heavy can matter become? Where does the periodic table end? These fundamental questions motivate my research on the synthesis of heavy and superheavy elements.

fh_welcome.title: Welcome
paragraphs: My research investigates the formation of superheavy nuclei in heavy-ion collisions and the fundamental limits of nuclear stability. Through reaction modelling, uncertainty quantification and scientific computing, I develop predictive frameworks for experiments searching for new elements and exploring the limits of the periodic table.
Alongside nuclear physics, I develop computational methods for scientific modelling, data-intensive computing and machine learning applications in physics.
